title: Card College
author: Roberto Giobbi
about: The standard structured course in sleight-of-hand card magic. Where most magic books are collections, this one is a curriculum: technique introduced in order, each volume assuming the last. It is the book most often handed to someone who asks where to start and still worth returning to years later.

title: Strong Magic
author: Darwin Ortiz
about: Ortiz on performance rather than method. The argument is that technical perfection is not what makes magic land, and that most performers fail at audience management long before they fail at sleights.

title: Designing Miracles
author: Darwin Ortiz
about: A study of how spectators reconstruct what they saw after the fact, and how to design effects that survive that reconstruction. Closer to cognitive psychology than to a trick book.

title: The Annotated Erdnase
author: Darwin Ortiz
about: Ortiz's annotated edition of The Expert at the Card Table, the 1902 text that remains the foundation of card table artifice and whose authorship is still disputed.

title: Scarne on Card Tricks
author: John Scarne
about: A large collection of card tricks requiring little or no sleight of hand, and a demonstration that method and impact are not the same thing.

title: The Magic Way
author: Juan Tamariz
about: Tamariz's theory of false solutions: the idea that a strong effect closes off every explanation the spectator reaches for, one at a time, until none is left.

title: The Five Points in Magic
author: Juan Tamariz
about: A short book on the performer's physical instrument: eyes, voice, hands, body, and what Tamariz calls the heart.

title: The Magic Rainbow
author: Juan Tamariz
about: Tamariz's broadest theoretical work, on what magic is for and what it does to the person watching.

title: Mnemonica
author: Juan Tamariz
about: The stack, and the case for memorized deck work. A full system rather than a single arrangement.

title: The Classic Magic of Larry Jennings
author: Larry Jennings

title: The Phantom of the Card Table
author: Critical Edition
about: The Walter Irving Scott material, and one of the more contested episodes in the literature of card table work.

title: The Card Magic of Dai Vernon
author: Dai Vernon

title: The Dai Vernon Book of Magic
author: Lewis Ganson
about: Ganson's record of Vernon's work, part of the long project of getting a famously reticent performer into print.

title: The Essential Dai Vernon
author: Dai Vernon
about: Collects material including More Inner Secrets, Further Inner Secrets, Ultimate Secrets, Malini and His Magic, and Tribute to Nate Leipzig.

title: Revolutionary Card Technique
author: Ed Marlo
about: Marlo's foundational technical work, issued in separate chapters over a period of years rather than as a single volume.

title: The Books of Wonder
author: Tommy Wonder / Stephen Minch
about: Two volumes of routines and the reasoning behind them. Wonder wrote about why a construction works as carefully as he wrote about how, which is rarer than it should be.

title: The Black & White Trick and Other Assorted Mysteries
author: Bruce Cervon / Mike Maxwell

title: Magic and Meaning
author: Eugene Burger & Robert E. Neale
about: Two performers arguing about what magic is actually doing when it works, and why the question matters to anyone who performs it.

title: Magic by Misdirection
author: Dariel Fitzkee
about: One of the three Fitzkee books, and an early attempt to treat misdirection as a subject with structure rather than a knack.

title: Modern Coin Magic
author: J.B. Bobo
about: The standard coin reference, and the book nearly every coin worker starts from.

title: David Roth's Expert Coin Magic
author: Richard Kaufman
about: Kaufman's record of Roth's work, which reset what close-up coin magic was understood to be capable of.

title: CoinMagic
author: Richard Kaufman
publisher: Published by Richard Kaufman and Alan Greenberg

title: Geoff Latta: The Long Goodbye
author: Stephen Minch & Stephen Hobbs
about: The posthumous record of a coin worker whose material circulated for decades largely by reputation.

title: Giacomo Bertini's System for Amazing Coin Magic
author: Stephen Minch

title: Coin Snatch / Thief of the Impossible
author: Paul Diamond

title: Gambling Sleight of Hand
author: Steve Forte
about: Forte's two-volume study of table work, written from inside the subject rather than about it.

title: 13 Steps to Mentalism
author: Corinda
about: The standard introduction to mentalism, organised as thirteen categories of method.

title: The Mental Magic of Larry Becker
author: Larry Becker

title: Magicana
author: Charlie Miller
about: Collected from Miller's long-running Genii column.

title: The James File
author: Allan Slaight
about: Slaight's enormous record of Stewart James, a man who invented far more than he ever performed.

title: Tarbell Course in Magic
author: Harlan Tarbell
about: Originally a correspondence course, later the eight-volume set that functioned as the general reference for most of the twentieth century.

title: Apocalypse
author: Harry Lorayne
about: Lorayne's monthly, bound into volumes.

title: The Jinx
author: Theodore Annemann
about: Annemann's magazine, and the source of a large share of the mentalism that followed it.

title: Fred Kaps Magic Circle lecture
author: Fred Kaps
about: The lecture material, transcript and audio together.
